subject: blue crab
title: Baby Blue Crabs Face 1 Main Killer for 37 Years: Other Blue Crabs

scenes.text: Baby blue crabs have one deadly enemy. It isn't a fish.
For thirty-seven years, scientists in Maryland tethered young blue crabs and watched what came.
Fish mostly swam past. Sonar showed the attackers were adult blue crabs.
Nearly every attack was cannibalism. Four in ten young crabs carried the marks.
In water two feet deep, the smallest had up to an eighty percent chance of being eaten in a day.
Their only refuge is the shallows. A blue crab's worst enemy is another blue crab.

description:
A 37-year Smithsonian study in Chesapeake Bay found that predation on tethered young blue crabs came from other blue crabs, not fish.
Signs of cannibalism showed up on 42% of the crabs, and the smallest ones in deeper water were eaten 60 to 80% of the time.
Did you know crabs ate their own kind this much?
first_comment: Seawalls are wiping out the shallow water where young crabs hide. Would you have guessed their biggest threat was their own kind?
